Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government data exchange systems. 25 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Integration of farmer registries, agricultural input vouchers, land registrations, extension services data
Comments: The Commonwealth Secretariat and Government of Malawi co-hosted a multi-stakeholder dialogue in 2023 on national data infrastructure for climate and agriculture DPI. Farmer subsidies use the national ID system for eligibility. Specific interoperability with a central data exchange layer for agriculture is under development.
revision_notes: Original sources (a 2023 blog on a Commonwealth Secretariat multi-stakeholder dialogue, and a 2022 UNDP piece on the general national ID system) describe early exploratory discussion and the ID system in general terms, not documented agriculture-specific integration outcomes, so the 'Under development' score understated actual progress. Fresh searches found: the Ministry of Agriculture's National Agriculture Management Information System (NAMIS) had, by December 2024, registered and geo-mapped over 3.4 million farming households and their land parcels (Nyasa Times); the 2025/26 Affordable Input Programme (AIP) reform assigns each beneficiary a digital ID linked to their national ID card and farm GPS coordinates (Nyasa Times, Sept 2025); a new e-voucher system built on a digital farmer registry is piloting data-driven subsidy allocation in 12 districts (World Bank, Oct 2025); and the Ministry of Lands' Land Information Management System (LIMS) is being built for API integration with the National Registration Bureau, National Statistical Office and Malawi Revenue Authority. This is genuine, operational (if partial) integration, so the score is revised upward to 4 (Partially integrated).
revised_comments: Malawi's Ministry of Agriculture operates the National Agriculture Management Information System (NAMIS), which by December 2024 had registered and geo-mapped over 3.4 million farming households and their land parcels, replacing paper-based farmer records. Verification for the Affordable Input Programme (AIP) increasingly draws on the national digital ID system: the 2025/26 AIP reform assigns each beneficiary a digital ID linked to their national identity card and farm GPS coordinates to eliminate duplicate and ghost claims. A new e-voucher system built on a digital farmer registry is piloting data-driven subsidy allocation in twelve districts. Separately, the Ministry of Lands' Land Information Management System (LIMS) is designed for API-based integration with the National Registration Bureau, National Statistical Office and Malawi Revenue Authority. These initiatives show genuine, though still partial, integration of farmer registry, land and identity data across agriculture-related systems; full nationwide interoperability across all agriculture data domains has not yet been achieved.
